messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: latency SLO breach detected for /v1/streaming endpoints · p95 spikes > 1200ms, p99 ~ 3500ms, streaming stalls observed. Severity: P1. Auto-page to #incidents.

alice (oncall): I'm on it. Seeing spike started ~ 2026-03-14T18:02:xxZ. p95 jumped from ~220ms to 1.2s, p99 ~3.5s. Throughput steady. No obvious backend errors, looks like tail latency (streaming stalls + token emission gaps).

bob (sre): Can you paste the dashboard links? Also check cache hit rates for prefix cache and KV store.

alice (oncall): Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/streaming/streaming-latency
Prefix cache metrics show huge miss rate on keys starting with "chat:stream:prefix:". Yesterday hit-rate ~97%, now ~44% across the cluster.

infra-monitor: ALERT: prefix-cache miss_rate increased 8.2x over baseline (1h) for service=streaming. Eviction count spike correlated with deploy at 2026-03-14T02:15Z.

carol (eng-runtime): I was about to say — we had a rollout last night that changed the KV hashing function (commit 8f3a2d). The goal was more even shard distribution but it changed key normalization for prefix keys (we removed a trim step). Could that rekey everything and cause misses? Commit: https://git.redwood/eng/runtime/commit/8f3a2d

alice (oncall): That matches timeline. If hashing changed, caches would see new keys -> cold misses -> tail latency. Streaming sessions rely heavily on prefix caching for KV lookups during token generation.

bob (sre): Can we confirm by sampling cache keys? Run a quick query to compare current cache keys vs previous pattern.

alice (oncall): Running a quick grep on prefix-cache logs...
```bash
kubectl logs -l app=prefix-cache -n prod --since=30m | grep "key=" | sed -n '1,60p'
```
Output snippet:
```
key=chat:stream:prefix:session:abc123
key=chat:stream:prefix::session:abc123   # double-colon anomalies
key=chat:stream:prefix:session:def456
key=chat:stream:prefix: session:ghi789  # leading space
```

alice (oncall): Looks like normalization rules changed; we now have keys with unexpected whitespace and extra separators. That would massively reduce hit-rate.

carol (eng-runtime): Confirmed — the trim() call was accidentally removed in one of the helper routines when refactoring. My bad. The deploy rolled out to 80% last night. I can prepare an emergency rollback of that helper change.

dave (product): Quick customer impact check: do we have affected customers with strict latency SLOs? CS pinged saying AcmeCorp reported stalls in the demo environment.

alice (oncall): Per request logs: top impacted tenants (by increased p99): AcmeCorp (tokens/sec drop), NovaSearch (replay stalls), internal smoke tests. Error rates are low; it's mainly timeouts and slow streaming answers.

bob (sre): Mitigations to consider now: 1) rollback the helper commit -> restores key normalization and hit-rate; 2) force TTL-based cache warmup by pre-seeding popular keys; 3) temporarily increase cache size / reduce eviction aggressiveness; 4) route streaming traffic to fallback nodes that still have warm caches. Which is fastest?

carol (eng-runtime): Fastest is rollback. I can cut a rollback PR and trigger canary. Alternative: a hotfix that reapplies trim() and roll forward — but rollback is simpler for emergency. If ops want to avoid full rollback, we can push a light re-normalization layer that rewrites keys on read to canonical form (hotfix) — but that'll be slower initially.

alice (oncall): We need immediate customer relief. I recommend rollback to 8f3a2d-1 (previous deploy) in the next 5-10 minutes and then validate hit rate.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued by carol. Image: runtime-prefixcache:v2026-03-14-abc. Rolling deploy to canary (10%) now.

bob (sre): While canary runs, let's also pre-seed top prefixes to reduce cold miss pain. alice, can you generate a list of top 500 keys and seed them? Use the seeder job:
```bash
kubectl run cache-seeder --image=registry.redwood/cache-tools --restart=OnFailure --namespace=prod -- \
  --top-n 500 --prefix "chat:stream:prefix:" --target prefix-cache
```

alice (oncall): Seeder kicked off. I'll watch hit-rate.

alice (oncall): Canary is green? Preliminary: canary nodes show hit-rate jumped to 95% and p95 down to ~240ms on canary. Good sign.

deploy-bot: Canary success. Rolling full rollback to 100% now.

alice (oncall): Hit-rate across cluster climbing: 45% -> 88% over 6 minutes. p95 improving: 1.2s -> 310ms. p99 trending down: 3.5s -> 420ms and continuing to improve. Streaming stalls dropping.

dave (product): Notifying CS and affected customers: AcmeCorp, NovaSearch. Drafting message: "We experienced increased latency on streaming endpoints due to an internal cache key normalization change; we’ve rolled back the change and are monitoring. No data loss. We expect full recovery in ~15 minutes."

bob (sre): Quick follow-ups: need a postmortem to cover deploy gating, integration tests for key normalization, and a canary rollout threshold tuned for cache miss signals. Also consider a metric alert on sudden cache key pattern deltas (separator/whitespace anomalies).

carol (eng-runtime): Will own rollback PR retrospective and submit a hotfix with normalization tests. Also adding a lint that prevents removal of normalization helpers.

alice (oncall): Handoff: I'm leaving at 19:10 UTC. Handoff to bob (sre). Current state: cluster hit-rate 92%, p95 ~260ms, p99 ~380ms. Seeding job finished. Observability: continuing to monitor for 30m.

bob (sre): Taking over. I'll keep the channel open and escalate if any regressions.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated - rollback deployed at 2026-03-14T18:09Z, customer notifications sent. Monitoring for recurrence.

dave (product): Great runbook items for postmortem. Also let's add a customer-facing post-incident note to explain impact and remediation.

alice (oncall): Thanks team. Leaving short notes in the incident tracker.

bob (sre): Closing checklist: confirm no residual invalid keys older than TTL, schedule a small job to scrub malformed keys in a safe, rate-limited manner. I'll open a ticket.

carol (eng-runtime): Ticket created: ENG-5482 "Normalize existing prefix-cached keys and add tests".

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: last_message_ts=1798124020. Time to recovery ~7 minutes from mitigation start. Root cause: kv hashing/key normalization change introduced in runtime commit 8f3a2d.

alice (oncall): Thanks everyone. Will draft the postmortem and include timeline, impact, and action items.

bob (sre): A note for ops: add an alert for cache hit-rate drops >20% in 5m and bucket by key pattern anomalies.

carol (eng-runtime): On it.

end of thread.
